analysis: The PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date on line 3 and adds one table row near head line 572 documenting a CPU-only `--prompt-prep` benchmark mode. The three supplied units are BASE text for lines 831-1806, which lie outside the changed ranges, so the new row at head line 572 is visible only as a patch excerpt. From the excerpt, the documented mode loads only the tokenizer, performs no network calls, does not touch keys or attestation, and writes no cache artifacts. It reads no coordinator or consumer data and prints JSON locally. It touches no asset or trust boundary in the threat model: not the A-003/A-001 key and prompt custody, TB-002 WebSocket, TB-011 authorization, the fan helper, or the T-041 prefix-cache at-rest surface. The row mentions the prompt token cache with background comparisons off. I read this as an in-process benchmark comparison and not the encrypted SSD KV prefix-cache tier governed by T-041. The base text I examined has no implied control change, and the surrounding documentation (logout, unenroll, cache env passthrough, App Attest worker opt-in) is unchanged. Remaining limit: I did not see the Swift implementation of PromptPreparationBenchmark. If it ships a prompt-token cache that persists prompts to disk, that code needs separate review against T-041/A-001, but the documentation change alone provides no evidence of that.
